description: Grade 5 example: write an interval under a key signature (Ab major, treble clef).

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 10 addendum)

item.prompt: The key signature of Ab major is shown. Write the note a minor 3rd up from this note, adding an accidental only if the key signature does not already give it.

music.textAlternative: One minim, Eb4, under the key signature of Ab major.

hints: Find the letter name first, then decide what the interval needs on that letter.
Then compare with the key signature: write a sign only for the difference.

feedback.correct: Correct. E♭ up a minor 3rd is G♭. A♭ major has B♭, E♭, A♭ and D♭ but not G♭, so the G♭ needs its own flat sign.

mistakes.redundant-or-missing-accidental: E♭ up a minor 3rd is G♭. A♭ major has B♭, E♭, A♭ and D♭ but not G♭, so the G♭ needs its own flat sign.
mistakes.accidental-not-applied: Check what the key signature already gives that letter before adding a sign. E♭ up a minor 3rd is G♭. A♭ major has B♭, E♭, A♭ and D♭ but not G♭, so the G♭ needs its own flat sign.
mistakes.enharmonic-spelling: That sounds the same but uses the wrong letter name. An interval's number fixes the letter: count the letter names from the starting note.

feedback.fallback: E♭ up a minor 3rd is G♭. A♭ major has B♭, E♭, A♭ and D♭ but not G♭, so the G♭ needs its own flat sign.
